units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration tests for selecting plugin-provided execution environments, acquiring/releasing leases through the Heartbeat path, applying instance defaults and Agent overrides, and rejecting stale non-reused workspace environment selection.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat resolves Environment precedence from instance/Agent/Work/workspace state, looks up a ready plugin manifest/driver, calls PluginWorkerManager environmentAcquireLease/environmentReleaseLease, passes lease context toward adapter execution and records workspace/environment projections.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest capability and environment driver schema, instance- or Company-scoped Environment with opaque driverConfig, instance defaultEnvironmentId, Agent defaultEnvironmentId, ExecutionWorkspace metadata/settings/mode, provider lease ID/metadata, Company/Issue/Agent/Run/adapter identity and remote cwd.
units.lifecycle: A selected plugin driver receives a lease request with environment/workspace/Work/Agent/Run/adapter context and returns provider identity/metadata; terminal execution releases it. A global instance default can serve Agents from different Companies unless an Agent explicitly overrides it. When a non-reused workspace contains stale environment metadata, the current assignee selection wins and a new execution workspace identity is sent to the provider.
units.testAssessment: Three broad integration cases cover acquire/release RPC shape, adapter type forwarding, global default across Companies, explicit Agent override and stale workspace environment replacement. Missing are real sandbox execution, database lease assertions, acquire/release idempotency, failure/timeout/cancel/crash and orphan cleanup, plugin restart/version upgrade, RPC authentication, provider attestation, Company authorization for global environments, secret/config isolation, schema validation, network/egress/filesystem policy, resource quotas, regional/data-residency constraints, concurrent leases and proof the adapter actually executes inside the leased environment. The manifest insert uses any and an unconstrained object schema.
units.designRationale: Make execution infrastructure extensible through plugin drivers, keep per-run adapter context visible to the provider, offer an instance-wide operational default with Agent-level exceptions, and prevent stale workspace metadata from overriding current assignment policy.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a neutral ExecutionEnvironmentPort spanning managed cloud, customer-local and hybrid nodes, with tenant isolation, data-egress policy, attestation and explicit selection precedence independent of any Agent vendor.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the capability-declared driver, typed acquire/release lease contract, per-attempt identity and explicit selection receipt. Replace opaque config and instance-global implicit sharing with versioned EnvironmentProfile, Company authorization, region/trust/data-egress/resource policies and secret references; global definitions may be templates, but each Company receives isolated credentials/leases. Require provider-signed runtime attestation, lease fencing/renewal/revocation, failure cleanup and compatibility tests. Environment selection should resolve Company policy → Work risk/data requirement → explicit approved override → Agent default, and record why stale workspace state was rejected.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is present but does not authorize environment choice or cross-Company default use. Plugin readiness and a returned providerLeaseId are trusted without isolation or execution proof; opaque driverConfig may contain secrets or policy-changing fields. Selecting a new Agent environment while reusing Work/workspace state has no accountable handoff or data-contract re-evaluation.
